newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares, hurt by market disinterest, ended flat to slightly firmer in mixed trade on Thursday, while a bookover deal in Investec Investment Trust Ltd (Intrust) ITTJ. pushed volumes higher at the close, dealers said.
The dealers said the bookover involved some seven million shares worth around 60 million rand and pushed the stock 20 cents up to finish at 820 cents.
"The market has just drifted off after a few good days of running. There are a few shares in the market that are going around but it's on very selective buying," one dealer said.
The industrial index was last down 2.6 points to 8,502.1, golds down 16.2 points at 1,147.8 and the all-share up 6.6 points at 7,292.7.
Despite the market's overall tardiness volumes were good with dealers saying around 836 million rand worth of shares had changed hands by the close of trade.
In the broader market decliners led advancers by 187 to 173 and 35 shares hit new highs while 28 sank to new lows.
The dealers said a slight recovery in the afternoon could have been spurred by arbitrage deals as futures players started to take positions ahead of the futures close-out next week.
"This morning the market was down, but it now seems to have made a slight come back," a dealer said.
"I think it's probably arbitrage transactions that are taking place, guys selling futures and buying shares because they've been trading quite far by fair value," he added.
Dealers said golds were shunned through most of the day on the bullion price hitting staunch resistence at the $344 level.

In stark contrast to golds the financial sector of the market was still awash with hopes of an interest rate cut later this year as the all-financial index hit another fresh year high. The index was last up 43.6 points at 9,783.5.
Dealers expected Friday's trade to be little unchanged.

"Tommorrow I think you'll see the same kind of pattern, very strong on the financials and very mixed on the industrials," one dealer said, adding Wall Street's response to a positive slide in U.S. May retail sales by 0.1 percent would also be considered.
The Dow was up 66.17 points at 7,641.33 by 1512 GMT.
"America seems to be pretty positive with those figures which came out and I think we could go a little better. They were well received here," he added.

Among other features on the stock market was De Beers which added 275 cents to 164.00 rand, industrial firm Toco Holdings which shed six cents to a new year low of 42 cents on continuing worries on the groups' earnings.
Industrial giant Barlows lost 25 cents to finish at 47.65 cents while pulp and packaging company Sappi was last unchanged at 48.25 rand following a roaring start.
Gold mining house, Vaal Reefs ended off 500 cents at 265.00 rand.

On the futures side, the June South African share futures started weaker in thin trade, hurt by a weaker bond market but by Thursday afternoon they managed to retrace some losses on the interest-rate bullish U.S. data, dealers said.
The June industrial contract was last at 8,145/48 from 8,183 settlement, the June gold contract at 798/810 from 816 and the June all-share contract at 6,545/55 from 6,568 settlement.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
